newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech police charge 11 in Agrobanka probe.
newsitem.headline: Czech police charge 11 in Agrobanka probe.

text.p: Czech police detained and charged with fraud and related offences 11 persons on Tuesday night in connection with an alleged 137 million crown ($4.5 million) fraud at the troubled bank Agrobanka a.s., an investigator said on Wednesday.
Deputy director of the Czech Investigation Bureau, Frantisek Kudej, told Reuters investigators would decide soon whether they would seek custody for the suspects or release them pending trial.
He declined to name the suspects or companies involved in the alleged fraud.
"Banking operations unfavourable for Agrobanka occurred involving 1.9 billion crowns, causing 137 million crowns in damage to the bank," Kudej said.

Agrobanka, the largest Czech fully private bank, has been under forced administration by the Czech National Bank (CNB) since a liquidity crisis last September, which evolved after a loss of depositors' confidence after the bank was taken over by secretive investment group Motoinvest.
Agrobanka said in a statement that its administrator had not been informed about any moves by the investigating authorities.

Agrobanka suffered losses reaching some nine billion crowns last year. The central bank plans to spin off its non-performing assets and sell the healthy part to a strategic foreign investor. HSBC is arranging the selloff.
-- Jan Lopatka, Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003 ($ = 30.30 Czech Crowns)
